header:
The Chemistry of As, Sb, and Bi
The pnictogens are a familiar group of elements. N and P are well known for their wide range of applications in organic chemistry; As, Sb, and Bi can likewise bond to carbon and form many interesting compounds.

subquestions.text_open: 7.1 The positive trivalent oxidation state is common among the pnictogens. Their lone pairs and vacant d orbitals give them Lewis basicity and acidity of varying strength. 7.1.1 In sharp contrast to $NR_3$, the inertness of the 6s electrons makes $BiR_3$ a rather weak base with poor coordination ability, although it can sometimes form complexes. The neutral complex A and the monocation B both contain a $BiPh_3$ ligand. In A, the mass fractions of Bi and the central metal Cr are 33.05 % and 8.22 %, respectively; in B, the mass fractions of Bi and the central metal Fe are 33.86 % and 9.04 %, respectively. The central metals in both A and B obey the 18-electron rule, and both complexes contain CO ligands. Write the chemical formulas of A and B.
7.1.2 Considering the structures of A and B, explain why the Bi-M bonds in them are stable. (No more than 50 words.)

7.1.3 Compared with $BiR_3$, $SbR_3$ is slightly less acidic but markedly more basic, which enables a wider variety of reactions. Mixing equimolar amounts of $Me_2SbBr$, $Me_3Sb$, and $MeSbBr_2$ does not give mixed products from methyl-group exchange; instead, a 2:1 ionic compound is obtained. Both its cation and anion contain two Sb atoms. The cation contains no Br, and the anion has a center of symmetry. Write the SMILES representations of the cation and anion separately, and state the geometry at each metal center.

7.2 Reaction of $SbF_2OTf$ or $SbF(OTf)_2$ with the ligand $^{Dipp}BIAN$ (structure shown below) in $CH_2Cl_2$ gives the five-coordinate Sb complex $SbF_2(^{Dipp}BIAN)OTf$ or $SbF(^{Dipp}BIAN)(OTf)_2$, respectively.
7.2.1 Use VSEPR theory to predict the molecular geometry of $SbF(^{Dipp}BIAN)(OTf)_2$.
7.2.2 The Sb-O bond in $SbF_2({}^{Dipp}BIAN)OTf$ is longer than that in $SbF({}^{Dipp}BIAN)(OTf)_2$. Briefly explain why.

7.2.3 Replacing $F^-$ with $N_3^-$ greatly decreases the stability of the product. After $Sb(N_3)(^{Dipp}BIAN) (OTf)_2$ is left overnight in a protic solvent, its proton NMR spectrum shows that it has decomposed to form a new cation. This cation contains no Sb and contains a special five-membered ring in addition to the five-membered carbon ring in $^{Dipp}BIAN$. Write the SMILES representation of this cation; a textual description may be used to supplement the structure.
